title: What About Bob?: Baby Steps to Madness
description: A self-help bestseller, a goldfish in a jar, and a therapist at the end of his rope—five steps into Bob Wiley's summer.
imageHint: Therapist's office in disarray with patient causing comedic mayhem and doctor looking exasperated

questions.question: Dr. Leo Marvin's bestselling self-help book gives his new patient, Bob Wiley, a mantra for life. What's the book called?
choices: I Feel Good, I Feel Great
questions.explanation: Bob's other mantra, "I feel good, I feel great, I feel wonderful," is the film's first line. Tom Hanks was Disney's first choice for Bob, and Woody Allen was in talks for Leo.

questions.question: Baby-stepping his way onto a bus, Bob follows Leo on his family vacation to what New Hampshire getaway?
questions.explanation: It was actually filmed at Smith Mountain Lake in Virginia. Winnipesaukee locals were upset, and New Hampshire's film commission complained the movie made them look "tacky."

questions.question: Bob arrives at Lake Winnipesaukee with a goldfish in a jar hanging around his neck. What's the fish's name?
questions.explanation: "Good morning, Gil. I said, good morning, Gil." Bob talks to Gil more kindly than Leo ever talks to Bob, and it's Gil who gets him through the bus ride north.

questions.question: With Gil safely ashore, Leo's son ties Bob to a mast and he drifts across the lake, conquering his fear by shouting what?
questions.explanation: "Isn't this a breakthrough, that I'm a sailor? I sail?" Bob drifts into the marina to a cheering crowd. The next morning he steals Leo's Good Morning America interview too.

questions.question: Bob's sailing triumph pushes Leo over the edge. He straps 20 pounds of black powder to his patient and calls the cure what?
questions.explanation: "Death Therapy, Bob. It's a guaranteed cure." The closing card: Bob became a psychologist and wrote a huge bestseller called Death Therapy. Leo is suing him for the rights.

easterEgg.title: Leo wasn't acting
easterEgg.text: Murray and Dreyfuss really didn't get along. Murray: "I drove him nuts, and he encouraged me to drive him nuts." Dreyfuss: "I don't like him, but he makes me laugh even now."
